messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager (infra-high) triggered for inference-5xx spike in us-west-2a. Alert: inference-5xx-rate > 2% over 10m.
sara: Im taking the page. early customer reports: higher latency and 502/504s on text-generation endpoints.
mike: confirmed metrics: anomaly only in us-west-2a; other AZs normal. Can you pull target group health?
sara: on it. `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:tg:... --region us-west-2` shows ~18% unhealthy instances in us-west-2a, healthchecks timing out.
ryan: running `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide` pods on hosts i-0abcde1234/ i-0fghij5678 show connection errors in kube-proxy logs.
kevin: CloudWatch ENI metrics: TXDropped/TXErrors spikes for those instances. Looks like network offload issues at host level.
ora: CS chiming in: two enterprise customers on Dedicated pools reported request failures and raised P1. They need ETA.
sara: telling CS: "Investigating a zonal NIC/network degradation in us-west-2a; steering traffic away and mitigating." will post update in 20m.
mike: short-term mitigation plan: 1) deregister affected targets from NLB 2) shift route weights to us-west-2b/c 3) engage AWS support. Keep KV cache impact in mind.
sara: starting drain sequence. Will remove lowest QPS hosts first to reduce KVCACHE cold starts. Command: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:tg:... --targets Id=i-0abcde1234`.
ryan: confirming drains. Observing immediate drop in 5xx from ~3.6% to ~1.2% cluster-wide. us-west-2a still shows intermittent spikes.
kevin: traceroutes show large RTT jumps at first hop from controlplane to instance IPs. Could be hypervisor switch bug.
nora: CS note sent: "Were actively routing traffic away from affected hosts and working with AWS. Well follow up with an ETA within 2 hours."
sara: opened AWS support case 9876543210. Provided ENI metrics and `dmesg` excerpts. AWS asked for `ethtool -S eth0` output and ENI stats per instance.
mike: also enabling cross-AZ burst capacity and temporary traffic weight changes: `routingctl set-weight inference us-west-2b 60` etc.
ryan: watch item: draining causes KVCACHE misses -> some latencies up for requests routed to other AZs. Were seeing a small tail increase but overall success rate improved.
kevin: AWS replied: investigating a potential NIC firmware regression affecting a subset of hypervisors in us-west-2a. Theyre scheduling host remediation.
ora: Dedicated pools affected? yes, a small percentage of dedicated hosts in the AZ are impacted. Flagging accounts ops for SLA exposure.
sara: handoff: mike, Im handing pager. Ill stay reachable for escalation but stepping off primary. Summary: single-AZ network plane degradation -> ENI errors -> NLB health flaps -> 5xx. Mitigations: drained bad hosts, shifted traffic, opened AWS case.
mike: taking over. copying actions: 1) continue monitoring 2) coordinate with AWS for remediation timeline 3) approve stop/start only if AWS recommends and we can accept cache eviction.
ryan: note: stop/start will change private IPs and cause KVCACHE misses; prefer AWS host-level remediation first.
kevin: AWS suggested stop/start for immediate remediation on individual instances; they warned itll remap ENI.
mike: agree with conservative approach. Only perform stop/start on hosts that remain high-TxErrors after drain and after coordination with CS for Dedicated impact.
nora: sent interim CS update and status page entry. Customers asking for root cause and ETA.
sara: pls collect and attach: kernel logs, `ethtool -S` outputs, CloudWatch ENI metrics, instance serial logs to the support case.
mike: assigning ryan/kevin to metrics dump. Nora to continue customer comms. Julia not present? replaced by nora for this thread.
kevin: metrics attached to case. AWS assigned a case owner and scheduled host remediation window; ETA currently "investigation in progress, remediation may take 1-3 hours".
ryan: monitoring: no new unhealthy hosts after drain. 5xx% stabilized at ~0.6% cluster-wide; us-west-2a still slightly elevated.
mike: will keep route weights shifted for next 4 hours as precaution. initiating infra change to make fallback prefer cross-AZ for 24h: CHG-2026.
sara: please log Dedicated SLA exposure for accounts with committed capacity in us-west-2a.
nora: logged to accounts-ops and notified impacted customers.
kevin: AWS advised hosts will be evacuated and hypervisor patched; they recommended we avoid any stop/start unless necessary.
mike: plan for next steps: 1) wait for AWS remediation, 2) if AWS requests instance action, coordinate stop/start on drained hosts only, 3) prepare post-incident communication with timeline and RCA.
nora: CS will draft customer-facing postmortem once we have RCA.
ryan: creating incident ticket (INC-2471234) with timeline, metrics, and mitigation steps.
mike: if anything regresses Ill escalate to SRE lead. Otherwise Ill start drafting the internal timeline and runbook for RCAs.
sara: backbrief: thanks team. Handback to sara at 2471234700 if needed.
incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigation in progress; monitoring.
